## Statistics (Phase 3 §2.1): estimands, units, intervals
- **Estimands.** The headline table reports, per (arm, operating point), the *favourable attainable latency*: the median over three process restarts of each restart's min-of-medians (minimum over five 50-pass blocks of the block median). The "typical" column below reports the *typical latency*: the median over all 15 blocks of the block medians. Both are stated; the headline is the registered quantity (§5 of the registration); the typical latency is what a deployment sees on average.
- **Experimental units.** Process restarts are the independent units (fresh process, fresh compile/capture, fresh CUDA context); blocks are nested in restarts and passes in blocks. The matched pairs are paired at the block level: five alternating (a, b) blocks per restart in one process, so the pair difference is a within-process quantity.
- **Precision needed.** Claims of the form "arm X is 2× faster" or "C1 pays 19 % for graph breaks" need far less precision than rankings within 1 % (for example C3 vs H at 8 s, −1.7 %). The intervals below say which is which.
- **Method.** Non-parametric bootstrap, 10,000 resamples, seed 20260921: for headlines, resampling passes within blocks and blocks within each restart (the three restart groups are kept), giving **block-level** intervals; for matched pairs, resampling the five alternating blocks of each restart. These are block-level intervals: restart-level inference needs more restarts (E6, five per headline arm). No bootstrap over the three restart summaries is presented as restart-level uncertainty.
- **A/A block.** The Sep 20 evidence contains no A/A block (same arm alternated against itself); E6 adds one at both operating points. An A/A block detects spurious differences under the ABAB design; it validates no causal explanation.

## The "2× line" at 4 410 (§2.5(v))
The plan (Phase 3.2) reads: "Streaming 4410 (probe): Y ≥ 2× on wall over the best arm — reported, but pursued only if the owner reopens the streaming lane." Two readings exist. Reading A, a 2× speed-up: (wall + Y) / wall ≥ 2, i.e. Y ≥ T_wall. Reading B, half the wall: Z = Y / T_wall ≥ 50 %. For X1 at 4 410 (Y = C1 − C3 = 1.7109 ms, best-arm wall = H = 2.3386 ms): reading A gives (wall + Y)/wall = 1.732×, below 2×; reading B gives Z = 73.2 %, above 50 %. The Sep 20 LEDGER.md and execution report applied reading B ("meets 2× on wall") — LEDGER.md coded the threshold as Y ≥ T_wall × (1 − 1/2), which is reading B. **Which reading the registration meant is an owner decision (§5 of the handoff); until it is made, both readings are reported side by side and no row is described as meeting the streaming line.** Registration text: plan_ceiling_ledger.md Phase 3.2; code: fullmodel/ledger.py THRESH.

## What the boundary numbers are (§2.5(vi))
- **0.73 µs/node (graph)** and **4.88 µs/node (stream)** are the SLOPES of the unprofiled chain wall time T(N) against N for a dependent chain of trivial int32 Triton kernels (N ∈ {10, 100, 1000, 2000}, 20 timed repeats after 5 warm-ups; evidence/boundary_bench.json `fits`: trivial/graph slope 0.732 µs, intercept 2.398 µs; trivial/stream slope 4.883 µs). They are DEVICE-SIDE per-node costs as seen by the host clock across the whole chain: execution of the trivial kernel plus its inter-node dependency resolution, per node. They are not host launch costs.
- **0.58 µs/node (PDL graph)** is the same slope for the chain launched with programmatic dependent launch (Triton 3.4 `launch_pdl=True`, which sets `cudaLaunchAttributeProgrammaticStreamSerialization`; the kernel executes `griddepcontrol.wait` before its dependent load and `griddepcontrol.launch_dependents` after its store) and captured into a graph: evidence/boundary_bench.json `fits['trivial/pdl_graph']` slope 0.579 µs. `griddepcontrol.wait` / `.launch_dependents` are confirmed in the PTX of the compiled kernel (`pdl_ptx = True`); the SASS was not inspected on Sep 20 (E7). Whether any overlap actually occurs on SM120 is NOT established by a slope: E7's node-level trace is the test, and the programming guide states the overlap is opportunistic.
- **0.29 µs / 0.16 µs (graph / PDL-graph serial gap)** are the median idle gaps between consecutive kernels of the N = 1000 trivial chain in the node-level trace of a separate traced run (evidence/boundary_bench_trace_analysis.json `trivial/graph/N1000` gap 0.288 µs; `trivial/pdl_graph/N1000` gap 0.160 µs): the boundary cost with kernel execution excluded. These are the numbers the ledger's X10/X12 use.
- **Host-side launch cost** (NVIDIA's constant-time-launch distinction: CPU time inside `cudaGraphLaunch`) was not a registered quantity; the C3 trace's API rows give it as context: median `cudaGraphLaunch` duration for the 1142-node C3 graph at 8 s = 222 µs (evidence/traces/trace_C3_352800_trace_cuda_api_trace.csv, i.e. ≈0.19 µs per node), against NVIDIA's CUDA 12.6 figure of 2.5 µs + ~1 ns per node for a straight-line graph on an RTX 3060 — the C3 graph is not straight-line (two streams, n/a captured kernels), so the comparison is indicative only.
- **The NVIDIA device-side comparator**: 1,025-node straight-line graph executing in 567 µs on an RTX 3060 under CUDA 12.6 (≈0.55 µs/node) is the device-execution analogue of the 0.73 µs/node slope, not of the host launch cost.

## Which condition produces the weight re-casts (§2.5(viii))
Determined from the harness and the traces, not from memory (docs/phase3/00_first_message.md addendum; probe docs/phase3/probes/autocast_probe.py, output autocast_probe.out; engineering run on ml-beast GPU 4). The parameters leave `load_public_model` with `requires_grad=True` (672 of 674) and the timing loop enters one `torch.autocast` context per 50-pass block with the cache enabled, so in eager the C++ weight-cast cache is hit: per-pass fp16 copy kernels fall from ~700 (cache disabled or `requires_grad=False`) to 120. The per-pass re-casts measured as X6a exist only in the compiled arms, where Inductor traces the autocast parameter casts as `aten._to_copy` graph ops (420 parameter-only `_to_copy` calls per pass in the C3 wrapper at 4 410; the sixty 1536×1536 mask-estimator weights dominate the time) and cudagraph-trees replays them every pass. NVIDIA's CUDA-graph guide states the same mechanism ("the cast operation is part of the captured graph"). `torch._inductor.config.freezing=True` constant-folds exactly these casts (E1a).

## Vol. 1 eager figure versus the pod (§2.5(iv))
The Vol. 1 archive ("Melband Systems ML.md", 16 Sep 2026 export) is not in this repository, so its 55 ms eager figure cannot be cited here by file; the pod measured eager A at 62.275 ms (evidence/full_A_c352800_r*.json; median of three restart minima, block-level 95 % CI [62.256, 62.333]). Known differences that can move an eager wall by 10 %: host CPU and its single-thread speed (eager A launches 1,353 kernels per pass, so per-launch host time is part of its wall — the pod's vCPUs vs the Vol. 1 host), driver and image (580.178.04 / torch 2.8.0+cu128 on the pod), SM clocks (pod: 2805 MHz median in session 1) and whether Vol. 1 timed the full model under the same 5a protocol. **UNRESOLVED** until the Vol. 1 host, clocks and image are read from the archive by the owner; nothing here changes the pod's numbers.

## Decompositions (Phase 3 §2.2–2.4; trace-derived, MODELLED)
**X1 at 8 s (docs/phase3/x1/x1_decomposition_352800.{json,csv}; C1 and C3 node traces, per-pass medians).** Span difference C1 − C3 = 6.203 ms = input-staging copies 2.502 ms (63 kernels, 25.8 MB memcpy per pass) + lost fusion 3.447 ms (904 fused + eager elementwise kernels vs 791 fused) + GPU idle gaps 0.735 ms (96 `cudaGraphLaunch` calls per pass, host median 3.2 µs each) + GEMM/SDPA kernel-selection difference -0.484 ms; the parts sum to the span difference within 0.002 ms. The unprofiled matched pair is 6.741 ms: residual 0.541 ms is the profiled-vs-unprofiled difference (C3 perturbation ×1.013; C1's own perturbation was not measured).
**Pad-and-batch, C3 vs H at 352800 (docs/phase3/padbatch/decomposition_table.{json,csv}, region_times.csv, regions_and_arithmetic.json).** Net wall difference C3 − H = -0.495 ms (unprofiled; trace span -0.607 ms).
